title: KNN as CPU Base Learner for NBA Prediction with Feature Count Gate (<100f)

source.paper: Machine Learning Models for NBA Game Prediction

finding: Comprehensive benchmark of LR, Ridge, RF, NaiveBayes, KNN, SVM, Stacking, Bagging, MLP, AdaBoost, XGBoost for NBA prediction. AdaBoost ranked 2nd after XGBoost. KNN viable as a competitive CPU model specifically when feature count is small (<100f), where distance computation is fast.

proposal.feature_gate: Only evaluate KNN individuals with n_features < 100 (inference speed guard). Skip KNN for >100f individuals in GA eval loop.
proposal.expected_brier: ~0.230-0.240 (below LR+AdaBoost but provides search diversity at low feature counts)
proposal.cpu_cost: O(n*k*d) at inference — fast for d<100, slow for d>200. Gate required.
proposal.implementation: Add 'knn' to MODEL_TYPES list. In eval function: if model_type=='knn' and n_features>=100: skip/return None. Use KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=5, metric='euclidean', weights='distance').
proposal.prerequisite: AdaBoost + NaïveBayes must be validated first (vm-add-adaboost-naive-bayes-model-pool priority-56)

cross_fleet_applicability.political: P4, P7, P2, P5 — POL has 272 feature candidates vs NBA 3377; KNN at <100f will activate more often on POL islands

additional_references.title: Leveraging ML and DL for NBA Match Results
additional_references.finding: DL ceiling Brier ~0.221 matches fleet best 0.22012 — no CPU actionable improvement beyond current roadmap

additional_references.title: Forecasting NCAA Basketball with Deep Learning
additional_references.finding: NCAA context only, not NBA — noted for cross-sport transfer potential
